accessibilityStatement.title: cyAccessibility Statement
accessibilityStatement.description1: cyThis accessibility statement applies to Possession Claim Service (Frontend).
accessibilityStatement.description2: cyThis website is run by HM Courts & Tribunals Service. We want as many people as possible to be able to use this website. For example, that means you should be able to:
accessibilityStatement.description3: cyWe’ve also made the website text as simple as possible to understand.
accessibilityStatement.description4: cyAbilityNet (opens in a new tab) has advice on making your device easier to use if you have a disability.

list.item1: cychange colours, contrast levels and fonts
list.item2: cyzoom in up to 400% without the text spilling off the screen
list.item3: cynavigate most of the website using just a keyboard
list.item4: cynavigate most of the website using speech recognition software
list.item5: cylisten to most of the website using a screen reader (including the most recent versions of JAWS, NVDA and VoiceOver)

enforcementProcedure.title: cyEnforcement procedure
enforcementProcedure.description1: cyThe Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) is responsible for enforcing the Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018 (the ’accessibility regulations’). If you’re not happy with how we respond to your complaint, contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service (opens in a new tab).

feedbackAndContactInformation.title: cyFeedback and contact information
feedbackAndContactInformation.description1: cyIf you find any problems not listed on this page or think we’re not meeting accessibility requirements or, you need information on this website in a different format like accessible PDF, large print, easy read, audio recording or braille, contact:
feedbackAndContactInformation.description2: cyWe’ll consider your request and get back to you in 5 days.

technicalInformationAboutThisWebsitesAcc.title: cyTechnical information about this website’s accessibility
technicalInformationAboutThisWebsitesAcc.description1: cyHM Courts and Tribunals Service is committed to making its web applications accessible, in accordance with the Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) (No. 2) Accessibility Regulations 2018.

complianceStatus.title: cyCompliance status
complianceStatus.description1: cyThis online service is partially compliant with the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines version 2.2 AA standard, due to the non-compliances listed below.

non-accessibleContent.title: cyNon-accessible content
non-accessibleContent.description1: cyThe content listed below is non-accessible for the following reasons:

list.item1: cyHidden formatting rules: Input formatting requirements (like forcing decimals for whole numbers 000.00) are not stated upfront, causing validation failures. This fails WCAG success criterion 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (Level A).
list.item2: cyGeneric page title and links not explaining when opening new tab: Give no clear explanation of a page’s purpose or the behaviour on page load. This fails WCAG success criterion 2.4.2 Page Titled (Level A).
list.item3: cyMissing back-navigation: No clear navigation exists to return to the ’respond to claim’ task list without re-running the entire process. This fails WCAG success criterion 2.4.5 Multiple Ways (Level AA).
list.item4: cyErratic focus order: After the "Remove" button, focus drops off-page to an unselected file upload input before returning to the "Choose files" button. This fails WCAG success criteria 2.4.3: Focus Order (Level A) and 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA).
list.item5: cyRedundant links: The ’Check answers’ section contains adjacent ’change’ links with identical hidden names that target the same destination. This fails WCAG success criteria 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (Level A).
list.item6: cyGeneric form groupings: Form groups apply a generic <legend> markup instead of associating radio options to monetary inputs, relying instead on generic, repeated legends. This fails WCAG success criteria 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A) and 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (Level A).
list.item7: cyInconsistent heading implementation: Identical "Details given by..." sections are inconsistently marked up across pages (some as h2, some as h3, and some not as headings at all). This fails WCAG success criteria 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A).
list.item8: cyDuplicate regions: The page contains duplicate "Case issued" regions, with the second region failing to match the purpose of its underlying notification. This fails WCAG success criteria 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A) and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A).
list.item9: cyAccessible name for task list items includes the status tag: Voice control users may be impacted attempting to click on task list items as they are required to announce the status as it is added as hidden text. This fails WCAG success criteria 2.5.3 Label in Name (Level A).
list.item10: cyTranslation failure: The Welsh version of the page fails to translate the text content, and the language attribute (lang) remains incorrectly set to English. This fails WCAG success criteria 3.1.1 Language of Page (Level A).

whatWeAreDoingToImproveAccessibility.title: cyWhat we are doing to improve accessibility
whatWeAreDoingToImproveAccessibility.description1: cyWe are actively working to review and improve accessibility on our service.
whatWeAreDoingToImproveAccessibility.description2: cyWe continually run automated tests using aXe core as part of development practices and frequently complete easy checks using assistive technology.
whatWeAreDoingToImproveAccessibility.description3: cyWe frequently engage with the accessibility team to ensure yearly accessibility audits are conducted.

preparationOfThisAccessibilityStatement.title: cyPreparation of this accessibility statement
preparationOfThisAccessibilityStatement.description1: cyThis statement was prepared on 8th Sept 2026 following an evaluation of the web application to which it applies. The assessment was conducted by internal teams within the HM Courts & Tribunals Service organisation and associated IT suppliers.
preparationOfThisAccessibilityStatement.description2: cyThe statement was last reviewed on 16<sup>th</sup> Sept 2026.
